cases.family: A low drive under the middle of the lid: floor, lid, floor, lid, floor. The gaps shorten into the turn and lengthen on the way out; the loudest strike is the middle one.
The same aim with more power keeps every surface and note, and compresses and raises the whole swell.
Where the lid is nearly shut, the same exchange runs longer and faster before it lets go, then trails off.
Where the lid stands wide open there is room for one answer only: floor, lid, floor.
A slight diagonal crosses from one ramp to the other under the lid, so the floor note changes in mid-phrase.
A diagonal across two western lanes keeps the floor note and changes the lid note in mid-roll.
From the far left of the tee a crossing shot changes both the floor and the lid on its way through.
The mirror crossing from the far right walks the other way: different floor order, different lids.
The authored original opening enters above the ramp, so the lid speaks first and the exchange is inverted.
A harder, slightly raised drive skips once on the ramp, passes the slot behind the lid and strikes the bell squarely.
One lane east the same escape is caught between the bell and the top of the lid: a second exchange in the opening gap above, which slows and fades instead of swelling.
A lob over the lid strikes a bell first and is turned down onto the top of the lid: a two-note answer with no floor.
A soft raised shot falls into the mouth from above: a short, even exchange and a late last knock on the ramp.
A direct strike on the front edge of the lid: one loud chime and nothing else, room for another part.
Disappointing: the long western roll is cut off after two notes when a raised hard drive slips out through the slot and under the bells.
Disappointing: too little power never reaches the lid, and the ball only patters down the ramp at low energy.
A firm lob clears lid and bells and lands far beyond in silence.
A low outward miss reaches ground without sound.
